name: gsip
description: Open soil spectral reference library in development. Full GSIP app, backend, pipeline and modelling source for builders to run, fork and extend. Smartphone observations linked to instrument spectra and laboratory evidence for future open AI and soil maps.

paragraphs: GSIP is building an open soil spectral reference library, with smartphones as the accessible capture and sample-linking tool. The library connects camera observations and metadata to instrument spectra and verified laboratory evidence; open AI models and the soil map are downstream goals. Ordinary RGB phone photos are optical observations, not wavelength-resolved spectra. See the library specification and implementation sequence.

GSIP is not a laboratory replacement. Public outputs locate observations by k-anonymous H3 cells, never precise coordinates. Photos are sanitized before canonical storage and checked again before release.

requirements.text: You can use, fork, modify, self-host and extend the software under MIT, including in your own products.
The library CLI and synthetic demo need no GSIP account or production credential; follow the library guide to choose private output directories and run them.
